summary: Redwood (AE+SE) walked Neptune through Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and prefix/KV cache. Main goals: reduce per-token cost while meeting 150ms p50 latency SLO for chat completions. Jonah demoed cost model tradeoffs (batch size vs latency, KV cache hit rate impact). Agreed next steps: share config template, run perf tests on sample traffic, and reconvene after benchmark results.
topics: prefix/KV cache benefits and hit-rate assumptions
cost model: tokens saved vs cache memory/egress
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samira: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Samira from Redwood, i'll hand over to Jonah for the technical walkthrough in a few minutes — quick intro, Neptune team?
[00:00:12] Aisha: Hi Samira, Aisha here, head of ML at Neptune, with Mark on infra and Priya on product. We're evaluating ways to cut inference costs without breaking our chat latency targets.
[00:00:28] Samira: Great, that's exactly what Optimize is for. Jonah?
[00:00:31] Jonah: Cool, thanks. So agenda: batching strategies, prefix kv cache, cost model and some numbers you can plug in. I'll show a demo in the Console and then we can talk through tradeoffs.
[00:00:45] Mark: Quick q, our current stack is a mix of hosted and some in-house endpoints. We use GKE with autoscaled GPUs for big batches, so curious about host vs dedicated.
[00:01:02] Jonah: Noted. For the demo we'll assume a hosted route but the recommendations map to Dedicated pretty directly — batching, cache, quantization choices still apply.
[00:01:18] Jonah: Ok, slide-ish start: Why batching? Throughput efficiency—when you increase batch size you amortize attention/kernel overhead across tokens. But latency grows due to queueing. So we find a sweet spot based on your arrival distribution.
[00:01:40] Aisha: Our arrival is spiky — 200 qps bursts to 1k qps, typical request is 120 tokens prompt + model returns 60 tokens. p50 target 150ms, p95 can be up to 350ms.
[00:01:58] Jonah: Good details — that means tight latency SLO. For spiky workloads we recommend dynamic batching with a small max batch and a short batching window (e.g., 8-12ms) to capture micro-batching without hurting p50.
[00:02:15] Jonah: Demo: Console -> Optimize -> Batching. (screen share) Here you can tune policy: max_batch_size, max_wait_ms, and target_latency_percentile.
[00:02:32] Samira: Note: Optimize will suggest these values based on historical traffic if you upload traces.
[00:02:40] Jonah: Now KV/prefix cache. The idea: cache the KV (key-value) attention cache for repeated prefixes so you avoid recomputing prefix tokens. For chat that reuse system prompt or recent context, hit rates are often 30-70% depending on UX.
[00:02:57] Priya: Our product often prepends the same system prompt + a 1-2 sentence user context, so sounds like a good fit. Question: memory costs?
[00:03:10] Jonah: Yes, cache size scales with context length and model size. Rough numbers: for a 65B model with 4k context, a full KV cache can be ~2-4 GB per concurrent session if you store all layers; optimized quantized cache and shared prefix caches bring that down. For our cost model we balance cache memory vs tokens saved.
[00:03:33] Aisha: Can you give a concrete cost example?
[00:03:36] Jonah: Sure. Assume baseline hosted cost = $0.0035 per input token + $0.004 per output token (these are placeholder numbers, we'll map to your contract). If average prompt is 120 tokens and output 60 tokens, baseline per-call token cost is (120*0.0035 + 60*0.004) = $0.42 + $0.24 = $0.66.
[00:03:59] Jonah: If KV cache hit rate is 50% and half of the prompt tokens are cached (say 60 tokens), you'd save 60 * 0.0035 = $0.21 per call, dropping to $0.45. That's ~32% cost reduction on token charges.
[00:04:20] Mark: But there's memory and possible egress if using dedicated cross-region?
[00:04:24] Jonah: Exactly. If we use a shared prefix cache in-memory on the serving node there's extra RAM but no egress. If you want cross-region or external cache we might incur egress. For Dedicated we can colocate caches. Optimize's cost model lets you enter memory cost per GB-hour and expected hit rates.
[00:04:42] Priya: What about batching impact on latency?
[00:04:45] Jonah: Tradeoff: larger max_batch increases throughput and reduces per-token compute cost (better GPU utilization), but queueing increases p50/p95. For your p50 150ms target we recommend smaller batching window, and capability to set per-route latency SLO so Optimize auto-tunes. Example: with max_batch 8 and max_wait 12ms we measured p50 ~120ms, p95 ~300ms on a 2-GPU config for our sample workload. With batch 32 and max_wait 30ms p50 grew to 180ms but throughput doubled, cost/token down ~25%. So it's a policy decision.
[00:05:20] Aisha: Those numbers assume KV cache enabled?
[00:05:22] Jonah: Good catch. The p50 numbers above were with KV cache enabled and a 45% hit rate. Without cache p50 was about 1.1-1.2x higher because more tokens have to be processed each request.
[00:05:36] Mark: Any effect on GPU memory when enabling KV caching?
[00:05:40] Jonah:Yes, KV cache resides in GPU memory or CPU depending on config. For high hit rates we often keep it on GPU for speed; that increases GPU memory requirements but reduces compute. Optimize can simulate memory footprint. For your profile, enabling GPU KV cache for recent 2k tokens increased memory by roughly 8-12% but dropped compute by ~20% in our bench.
[00:05:58] Priya: And eviction strategies?
[00:06:00] Jonah: LRU or time-based TTL. For chat use-case LRU + per-session prefix buckets works well so recent context stays hot.
[00:06:08] Jonah: Now cost model in the Console: (screen share) you can toggle batch sizes, cache hit rate, memory cost, and it will show projected monthly spend and per-unit cost.
[00:06:20] Jonah: I'll plug in a toy example with Neptune numbers: 100k daily calls, baseline per-call $0.66 -> monthly ~ $1.98M (this is raw token cost estimate), with 50% cache hit and moderate batching you get down to ~$1.34M — about 32% savings.
[00:06:40] Aisha: Wait 100k daily calls -> $1.98M monthly seems high, check math?
[00:06:45] Jonah: sorry, math slip — you're right. 100k daily * $0.66 = $66k/day -> ~$2M/month. Ok numbers line up but we'll send the sheet so everyone's comfortable.
[00:07:00] Mark: Important: we have regulatory requirement to not persist user messages beyond 30 days. Does KV cache conflict?
[00:07:09] Jonah: No, you can configure cache TTL and automatic scrub or store encrypted in a customer-managed KMS. For Private deployments you can keep cache on-prem and we support KMS/HSM integration.
[00:07:21] Priya: How does this change for Dedicated?
[00:07:24] Jonah: Dedicated lets you reserve GPU pools, we can set pinned model + cache colocated. That reduces egress and often reduces per-token cost in our committed pricing. Optimize will model both hosted and dedicated scenarios — we can run a Dedicated projection given your committed capacity.
[00:07:37] Aisha: Are there degrade/fallback policies? If cache misses spike or memory pressure rises?
[00:07:43] Jonah: Yes, Redwood supports graceful degradation: fallback to smaller model variants, disable cache for some routes, or autoscale. Console has policy configs for fallback thresholds.
[00:07:55] Samira: Ok recap, we showed: batching knobs, KV/prefix cache benefits with sample numbers, memory cost tradeoffs, and how the cost model projects monthly savings.
[00:08:06] Aisha: Helpful. Can you include the exact benchmark scripts you ran?
[00:08:10] Jonah: We'll share the perf script and the CSV of latency vs batch size. Action: Jonah runs a 2-hour perf with your sample traffic once you share it.
[00:08:20] Mark: Also want to validate p95 end-to-end with our network. We'll do a joint run.
[00:08:25] Samira: Great — i'll send the Optimize template and the cost spreadsheet right after this.
[00:08:30] Priya: One more: how does conversation threading affect cache hit rates? We sometimes include 3-4 previous user messages.
[00:08:37] Jonah: Threading helps if prefix repeats. If each user is unique it lowers shared prefix hit rate. Optimize expects you to specify what part of the prompt is stable (system + template) vs per-user. That makes the simulated hit-rate more accurate.
[00:08:50] Aisha: Ok thanks, that clarifies a lot.
[00:08:53] Samira: We'll follow up with the docs and schedule. Thanks all.
[00:08:58] [00:48:00 end] Note: transcription contains minor mis-hears (e.g., "kv cache" sometimes transcribed as "kay vee cache"), filler words and occasional speaker label inaccuracies.
